definition: The XyloTron is an open-source, portable macroscopic wood identification system developed to support supply chain verification and the enforcement of laws against illegal logging.
details: The device uses computer vision wood identification models to classify wood specimens based on their macroscopic anatomy and requires minimal operator training. Designed for use in laboratory and field settings, the system provides a non-destructive method to rapidly identify wood. The system's accuracy depends on the quality of the training data, the breadth and anatomical complexity of woods in the model, and the similarity of unknown samples to those included in the model. Use of the XyloTron is intended to help establish probable cause in cases of possible illegal logging, rather than for high-stakes legal enforcement or forensic confirmation. Microscopic analysis of wood specimens by a wood anatomist may still be required.

explainer.lead: XyloTron is a portable, open-source system for identifying wood from its macroscopic anatomy. It matters because rapid field identification supports supply chain verification and enforcement against illegal logging.

tiers.eli5: It is a small box with a camera and a trained eye that looks at a piece of wood and names it, so inspectors can check wood on the spot without a lab.
tiers.practitioner: Operators capture images of a specimen and a computer vision model classifies the wood; the system needs minimal operator training and is non-destructive. A common pitfall is accuracy dropping when an unknown wood is anatomically complex or unlike anything in the training data.
tiers.paperLevel: The system classifies specimens from macroscopic anatomy images using computer vision models; accuracy is bounded by training data quality, the breadth and anatomical complexity of woods covered, and similarity of unknown samples to those in the model.

explainer.example: A field inspector photographs the end grain of a plank with the XyloTron, and the model returns the most likely wood class, flagging low confidence if the sample looks unlike the training set.
